Some of you older Voaters may be able to cast your minds back as far as the 1990's. At the start of the decade it seemed like it was the beginning of a bright new chapter in our world. The honeymoon period would not last long, however, and I think that there are a lot of parallels between the 90's and today.

The 90's, for all it's virtues, also brought a huge host of problems. Rodney King, a black taxi driver, was filmed being brutally beaten with batons by LAPD officers who were then acquitted of committing any crime. The acquittal led to the six day LA Riots as we became acutely aware that race relations in the US aren't as rosy as we would have thought. I think that this one is pretty self-explanatory given recent goings on in Missouri, NY, etc.

Tipper Gore, wife of Al Gore, listened to the lyrics of a Prince song and freaked out because it was about sex. She felt it to be her civic responsibility to protect the ears of everybody from sexually depraved or occult lyrics and created the PMRC. Ultimately all that was achieved was the parental advisory "Tipper stickers" that we see on album covers nowadays, but it was concerning to see music targeted as being a bad influence on children and society in much the same way as it is concerning to see the same argument rehashed today in regards to sex or violence in video games.

1999 saw the WTO Riots in Seattle as ordinary people stood up against globalisation that was being negotiated against their will. I'm hoping that it won't come to that again but the TPP and TTIP deals are as widely condemned in some circles so time will tell.

Now for some of the less serious parallels; 90's fashions such as flannel shirts and jeans with no knees have made a huge comeback, NWA are relevant once more, Suge Knight killed a man (again), kids are wearing Kurt Cobain t-shirts and there's a Clinton running for the presidency.
